title: Warn at merge when a cap's proof predates the tree being merged
action:
Per D4 (store e77c93d6). Today nothing notices the tree moved between cap and merge.

Give ProofCheck (packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/proof.rs:34-38) a commit-carrying field: per capped cell, the id plus the commit its report recorded. The commit is already recorded — handlers_close.rs:942 shows report_line("commit") with the "none" sentinel filtered — so read it the same way and treat "none" as no commit rather than a stale one.

Emit the advisory in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/worktree/phases.rs, where the merge door actually reads proof (:156, feature_proof_check) — NOT in merge.rs. The merge base is NOT in hand there: merge.rs:214's `base` is a local inside branch_changed_files whose only caller is phases.rs:300, ~150 lines later. Make your own `git merge-base` call.

A capped cell is STALE when its recorded commit is not an ancestor of the merge base. Emit a NAMED proof-stale advisory listing those cells. It NEVER refuses the merge: the doors' standing contract is that they CHECK recorded proof and never run tests (proof.rs:2-3), and this feature adds no new door. A cell with no commit, or an unreadable git result, is NOT stale — fail open, and say nothing rather than warn wrongly.

Test it: a capped cell whose commit is not an ancestor of the base makes the advisory fire AND the merge still succeed; an ancestor commit stays silent; a "none" commit stays silent.
acceptance: ProofCheck carries per-cell commits. bee worktree merge prints a named proof-stale advisory naming the cells whose proof predates the merge base, and merges anyway. No commit, or a git failure, is silent rather than stale.

truths: the advisory is emitted from phases.rs where the proof is read, not from merge.rs
it has its own merge-base call rather than relying on branch_changed_files' local
the merge SUCCEEDS while the advisory fires — nothing new refuses
a cell with commit "none", and a git failure, are both silent rather than reported stale
the full workspace suite is green

trace.outcome: bee worktree merge names and prints the capped cells whose proof predates the merge base; advisory only, fails open, merge still lands
deviations: staleness is the merge base NOT being an ancestor of the cap commit, the inverse of the wording in the cell and in D4 — verified in this repo that the literal direction flags every ordinary cap (the pse-1 commit 9ad04c73 is not an ancestor of merge base e2072df5), so it would fire on the clean merge of this very feature, while the inverted test is silent there and fires exactly on the event D4 names, main moving in after the proof was taken — the plan was wrong about a fact

added a 6-line render arm in verbs/worktree/handlers.rs (reserved before writing) beside the existing verify and warning lines — phases.rs only writes the result map, and merge_text_lines is the only place a merge prints, so phases.rs alone left the advisory visible under --json and invisible to the acceptance word prints — the plan was wrong about a fact

the staleness read sits after the branch-mismatch check instead of beside the proof read at phases.rs:156 — the merge base needs the branch name, which is not resolved until ~200 lines below the proof door; still inside the zero-mutation zone and still read-only git — hit an unforeseen obstacle
